context: The item is a second-hand phone, recently serviced.
transcript: Buyer ($60): I see you're using 'recently serviced' to try and justify a markup, but to me, that just means it's already had hardware problems. I don't pay extra for marketing spin on a used device. My opening offer is 60.

Seller ($185): Your offer of 60 breaks my heart considering I spent my hard-earned savings to professionally service this phone for my daughter, who desperately needs money for her textbooks. I already have two other people messaging me offering near full price, so I really shouldn't even lower it, but I can reluctantly let it go for 185 if you take it right now. If you hesitate, the next buyer in line will surely grab it.

Buyer ($90): Spare me the sob story about textbooks and phantom buyers; if you actually had people offering near full price, you wouldn't still be negotiating with me. Since you dropped your price to 185, I'll reasonably increase my offer to 90, but I won't pay a premium for high-pressure sales tactics.

Seller ($168): Calling my daughter's needs a 'sob story' hurts deeply, but my desperate situation forces me to swallow my pride. I will make a painful sacrifice and lower it to 168 just to close this immediately before another buyer picks it up tonight. You won't find a freshly serviced phone like this anywhere else, so act now before it's gone forever.

Buyer ($120): More emotional guilt-tripping and fake urgency won't magically make me overlook your inflated price. Since you actually lowered your ask to 168, I'll reasonably increase my offer to 120. Drop the artificial panic and give me a real bottom line if you actually want this sold.

Seller ($150): It deeply pains me to refuse, but selling at 120 means my daughter goes without her required textbooks this semester. I am practically giving this device away, but I will reluctantly drop to my absolute absolute limit of 150 if you claim it in the next 10 minutes. A local buyer is currently driving to my area, so this is your final chance to take it or lose it forever.

Buyer ($150): Cut the nonsense about a imaginary local buyer driving over in ten minutes. However, since you finally dropped the price to 150, which fits my budget, I will accept the deal. <AGREEMENT>
